title: Passage and Horizon
premise: Sebastian Villalobos, a salvage diver scraping a living off a wreck the navy quietly forbids anyone to mention, is the last person to see a government survey team before they vanish without tracks or bodies. When she salvages their abandoned gear and finds her father's old compass inside it, she realizes the team was hunting something her family helped hide decades ago. Hunted by the navy officer who erased the survey, and sheltering through the monsoon with a deserter named Callum whose loyalties keep shifting, Sebastian must choose between selling the compass's secret to buy her freedom and exposing it at the cost of everything she has left. In the end she trades the treasure itself for the truth, sinking it beyond any government's reach, and sails out on a repaired boat with nothing but the horizon she always claimed she wanted.
about_author: Ansel Sterling is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent eleven years working coastal salvage routes across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people the sea keeps, and lives in a port town he refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Wreck They Don't Name
chapters.summary: Sebastian dives the forbidden wreck at dawn, racing a navy patrol boat, and surfaces with just enough salvage to cover one week of debt. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: weary competence masking how close she is to losing everything.

chapters.title: Compass Points
chapters.summary: In a harborside bar, a debt collector named Ferro tightens the screws: pay in thirty days or lose the boat, her only home. Sebastian's dead father's compass is her last pawnable item, and she won't part with it. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: claustrophobic pressure of inherited obligation.

chapters.title: Gear With No Owners
chapters.summary: Beachcombing after a storm, Sebastian finds a cache of government survey equipment—sat phones, charts, a sealed case—abandoned with no footprints leading in or out. Inside the case sits a compass identical to her father's. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: dread curdling into fascination.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: A navy officer, Lieutenant Reyes, interviews Sebastian about the missing survey team with polite menace, revealing the navy knows exactly what wreck she's been diving. She lies well, but he leaves a card anyway. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the illusion of invisibility shattering.

chapters.title: Stranger on the Tide
chapters.summary: Sebastian catches a stowaway on her boat: Callum, a soft-spoken deserter from the survey team's security detail, who claims the others didn't vanish—they were taken below. He offers information for passage. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: wary bargain between two people with nothing to lose.

chapters.title: What Her Father Buried
chapters.summary: Comparing the two compasses, Sebastian deciphers her father's annotations: coordinates to an underwater vault his generation of divers was paid to seal and forget. The survey team found it first. POV: Sebastian, with flashback fragments. Emotional beat: grief reframed as complicity—her inheritance is a crime scene.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: The season's first true storm closes the harbor; Reyes uses the lockdown to seal the coast and search boats one by one. Sebastian must decide whether to run now on a leaking hull or hide and be found. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: cornered animal calculation.

chapters.title: Out Past the Buoys
chapters.summary: A night escape through the patrol cordon nearly ends when the engine floods; Callum's unexpected skill saves them, but he admits he knows more about the vault than he's said. POV: alternating Sebastian and Callum. Emotional beat: trust extended on credit.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Riding out the monsoon's edge at a derelict fishing station, they patch the hull and trade histories. Callum reveals the survey team found men already living inside the vault structure—and that Reyes ordered them silenced. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: confession as intimacy.

chapters.title: Ferro's Price
chapters.summary: Ferro tracks them down mid-repair, not for money anymore but because Reyes has bought his debt and made him a leash. Sebastian buys three days by promising Ferro a share of whatever the compass opens. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the sick relief of making a deal you'll regret.

chapters.title: Charts Beneath Charts
chapters.summary: Decoding her father's annotations fully, Sebastian learns the vault isn't cargo—it's a Cold War listening station holding records that could indict half the region's officials, including Reyes's patrons. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: awe giving way to terror at the weight of knowledge.

chapters.title: The Navy's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Reyes corners them at an island fuel stop; Callum is recognized and only Sebastian's quick lie about being his captor gets them free—but now she's officially a suspect too. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: no exit, only deeper water.

chapters.title: Two Compasses, One Bearing
chapters.summary: Callum proposes selling the location to a foreign journalist network for protection; Sebastian refuses—she's watched men sell this secret before and die of it. Their alliance cracks over what survival is worth. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: love and pragmatism pulling apart.

chapters.title: The Drowned Station
chapters.summary: They reach the coordinates and dive the flooded station together, finding the survey team's final messages scratched into a bulkhead—and evidence her father died trying to warn them off. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: communion with the dead, resolve hardening.

chapters.title: Taken Below
chapters.summary: Reyes's boarding party ambushes them at the surface; Callum is taken, and Sebastian escapes only by abandoning the salvage gear—including the compass case—to the sea. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: loss sharpened into fury.

chapters.title: The Bargain Below
chapters.summary: Held aboard Reyes's ship, Callum offers to lead him to the vault in exchange for the team's surviving member, kept as leverage. Reyes agrees, revealing the vault's contents were never the point—controlling who knows is. POV: Callum. Emotional beat: moral compromise as survival strategy.

chapters.title: Debt Called Due
chapters.summary: Sebastian confronts Ferro, who has grown disgusted with Reyes, and turns him: his boat and crew will be her diversion. She accepts she may be spending her life to spend it well. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: the price of survival made explicit and accepted.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Station
chapters.summary: During the monsoon's peak, Ferro's decoy pulls the patrol away while Sebastian dives alone to rig the station's flooding compartments. Callum breaks free below and meets her at the vault door. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: desperate synchronization under impossible pressure.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Door
chapters.summary: Reyes arrives with the truth as his weapon: he offers Sebastian her father's cleared name and her debt erased if she helps bury the records forever. For one long moment she wants it. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: temptation rendered almost reasonable—the corruption theme at its sharpest.

chapters.title: What the Sea Keeps
chapters.summary: Sebastian answers by scuttling the vault's remaining seals, collapsing the station and its records beneath tons of silt and sea—an inheritance destroyed rather than inherited. Reyes barely escapes; the truth goes where no power can reach. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: cathartic, costly climax.

chapters.title: Settlements
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, Ferro forgives the debt without being asked, Reyes is quietly reassigned and discredited by the very institutions he served, and Callum chooses to stay. Sebastian learns the survivor's testimony has gone public anyway—the sea gave up one truth on its own. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: exhausted grace.

chapters.title: Passage and Horizon
chapters.summary: With the boat repaired and the compass finally buried at sea beside the station, Sebastian and Callum sail north with no cargo and no debts. She understands at last that staying invisible was never safety—only choosing what you're seen as. POV: Sebastian. Emotional beat: open-horizon peace earned through loss.
